title: Time-Dependent Vector Fields
notes: Begin by positioning Appendix B as the calculus layer under contact isotopies. Students already know that a contact structure may be carried by an isotopy; here the question is how forms change when both the measuring map and the vector field depend on time. Emphasize that every later formula is a bookkeeping device for that motion.

title: Moving Maps
notes: Make the phrase vector field along the image precise. The point q in the source is fixed while its image j_t(q) moves through M. Differentiating that path gives a vector at j_t(q), so the equation X_t composed with j_t equals j-dot_t is a definition of velocity along the moving submanifold.

title: Lemma B.1 Pullback Derivative
notes: Present Lemma B.1 as the central computational identity. A pulled-back form changes because the map moves, not because alpha itself changes. The two Cartan terms separate the exact contribution from the contraction with d alpha. This is the appendix version of measuring motion through differential forms.

title: Why The Proof Works
notes: The proof is short because it refuses to treat time as mysterious. Lift the whole problem to the product cylinder M x R, where the time-dependent vector field becomes an ordinary vector field X plus partial_t. Then the usual formula for an ordinary flow can be restricted back to a time slice.

title: Time-Dependent To Ordinary Flow
notes: Use the displayed formula to distinguish two clocks. The variable h is ordinary flow time on M x R, while t names the slice where the point starts. The map first returns p to the time-zero flow chart, then advances it to t plus h, and finally records the new time coordinate.

title: Lie Derivative At Moving Time
notes: Now specialize to a flow psi_t generated by X_t and a fixed form alpha. Pulling alpha back by psi_t lets the observer sit on the initial manifold while the map moves. The derivative of that pulled-back family is exactly the pullback of the Lie derivative taken with the instantaneous vector field.

title: Cartan Formula Survives
notes: Stress the phrase freeze the time. For each fixed value of t, X_t is just an ordinary vector field on M, so the usual Cartan formula applies without amendment. Time dependence tells us which vector field to choose at each slice; it does not add a hidden time derivative to the operator.

title: Direct Product Proof
notes: Read the diagram from the cylinder downward. Exterior derivative and pullback commute, contraction is evaluated against the lifted vector field, and then restriction to the slice t returns the original time-dependent formula. The proof is a transportation argument: do ordinary calculus upstairs, then project the bookkeeping downstairs.

title: Convention Trap
notes: This warning prevents a serious notation error. The symbol L_{X_t} alpha_t differentiates alpha_t in the spatial direction X_t at a fixed time. It does not include the explicit variation of alpha_t with t. A transported time-varying form therefore has two terms: alpha-dot_t and the Lie derivative.

title: Contact-Topology Use
notes: Connect the appendix to the familiar Gray and Moser style equation without proving the theorem here. The task is to choose X_t so the transported derivative of alpha_t is controlled, often only up to multiplication by alpha_t. This is why separating alpha-dot_t from L_{X_t} alpha_t matters.

title: Recap Exercise
notes: Let students answer before revealing the pattern verbally. Case A uses the Lie derivative of a fixed form under a moving flow. Case B uses Lemma B.1 for a path of embeddings. Case C needs the total transported derivative, so both alpha-dot_t and the Lie derivative appear. The habit is to name what moves.
